target.title: Draft: add CLI catalog views
target.body:
## Summary

This draft implements the CLI catalog direction from the RFC:

- RFC PR: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/32
- RFC file: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/rfcs/blob/codex/cli-catalog-overlay-rfc/rfcs/0016-cli-catalog-overlay.md

It adds a read-only `openclaw catalog` inventory over existing OpenClaw command/tool surfaces. The catalog is not a dispatcher, policy engine, runtime hook, or replacement registry. Existing CLI commands, routed operations, plugin commands, tools, and node/operator paths still own validation, permissions, confirmation, execution, and results.

## Source Registry Additions

The source-registry change is intentionally small. Registries contribute only the operational facts that are hard to infer consistently:

```ts
type CommandEffectProfile = {
  effectMode: "read" | "mutating" | "mixed";
  confirmationRequired?: boolean;
  risk?: "low" | "medium" | "high";
  commandHints?: readonly string[];
};

type CatalogExposure = {
  tier?: "public" | "internal";
};
```

Plugin CLI descriptors can also mark placeholders as `hidden` so private/local surfaces stay out of generated catalog views unless explicitly requested.

CLI descriptors still own command shape, route entries still own routing/policy shape, plugin descriptors still own plugin command shape, and node/operator commands come from node pairing/runtime declarations. The catalog layer does the N-to-1 normalization into ids, source labels, ownership, lens membership, docs/prompt/audit/operator views, and derived summaries.

## Catalog Surfaces

This branch adds:

- `openclaw catalog list` JSON/Markdown output
- runtime Commander-tree inventory for the current invocation
- opt-in plugin descriptor and command-registration inventory with `--plugin-descriptors`
- supplied node/operator command metadata
- prompt projection, including a scoped `node-operator` prompt view
- audit, test-matrix, and operator summary views
- schema fixtures, generated docs, and advisory report artifacts

## Complexity This Makes Inspectable

Current branch fixtures exercise the catalog across:

- 61 CLI descriptors
- 97 command routes
- 14 routed operations
- 5 explicit agent/tool surfaces
- supplied node/operator command metadata

The catalog command distinguishes static descriptor data from dynamic runtime/plugin data: `openclaw catalog list` collects the live Commander tree for the current invocation, and `openclaw catalog list --plugin-descriptors` includes plugin-provided CLI descriptor metadata when explicitly requested.

This matters for Scout-style deployments because the loaded runtime is not a fixed static list. The Scout container proof already sees 13 plugins, 11 enabled plugins, 2 plugin CLI commands, 8 plugin tools, and 23 allowed command/tool names from loaded config.

## Scout / Node-Mode Evidence

The live node-mode motivation comes from `gim-home/m` work:

- `gim-home/m#4045`: node-routed MCP commands such as `mcp.help`, `mcp.invoke`, `mcp.status`, and `mcp.cancel`
- `gim-home/m#4086`: filesystem node commands such as `filesystem.read`, `filesystem.write`, and `filesystem.patch`
- `gim-home/m#4088`: browser/file-open node commands such as `browser.open` and `file.openWithDefaultApp`

A node-operating agent needs a small prompt view of available node commands, argument hints, risk, confirmation, and approval boundaries that match the actual Desktop/Gateway implementation. The catalog provides that view without dumping the full inventory into prompts.

## Review Stack

This rollup PR contains the catalog stack folded together for directional review. The same work is split into fork-local draft PRs so reviewers can inspect it one layer at a time:

- PR1 foundation: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/11
- PR2 dynamic/operator lenses: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/12
- PR3 prompt projection: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/13
- PR4 schema fixtures: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/14
- PR5 generated docs: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/15
- PR6 hardening and consumer contract: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/16

Those fork-local PRs are review aids, not a request to merge from the fork. I can open the same stack against `openclaw/openclaw` separately if maintainers prefer.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli-catalog-overlay/list.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/prompt-projection.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/plugin-commands.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/schema-fixtures.test.ts src/plugins/captured-registration.test.ts src/plugins/loader.cli-metadata.test.ts src/cli/catalog-cli.test.ts --reporter=dot`
- `npm exec -- oxfmt --check <review-touched files>`
- `git diff --check`
- Clean Codex review pass for PR1-PR6 and RFC PR #32 after the source-registry effect/exposure update
- Earlier stack validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/cli-catalog-overlay-list.test.ts test/scripts/generate-cli-catalog-doc.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/schema-fixtures.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/prompt-projection.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/list.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/operator-summary.test.ts src/cli/catalog-cli.test.ts --reporter=dot`

## Notes

This is a draft for maintainer feedback on the source-registry contract, catalog command shape, dynamic/plugin/node inventory boundaries, and whether to merge as one PR or as the smaller stacked PRs.
